subject: Renewal pricing: staged capacity onramp + rate guard
snippet: Agreement on a staggered commit with a temporary rate guard and a one-time credit tied to onboarding milestones.
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@auroraedge.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@auroraedge.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — looking for a safe ramp

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the renewal reminder — Samir and I reviewed our Q3 roadmap and the expected production traffic profile. We appreciate the flexibility Redwood offered during our initial ramp, and we want to set up a renewal that supports a predictable onramp without locking ourselves into an oversized commit in months 1–3.

High-level asks from our side:
- A staged commit that starts with a modest baseline for the first two months and ramps to target over the following quarter.
- A temporary rate guard (price hold) for the first 6 months while we finish model optimizations and prefix caching improvements.
- A one-time onboarding credit tied to operational readiness (we'll need time to shift some traffic).

Can you share a sample amendment (numbers + timing) and any constraints from Redwood's side? Ideally we can have a commercial sketch this week to route internally.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Head of ML Platform
AuroraEdge

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@auroraedge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — looking for a safe ramp

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks.

Summary of what Redwood can propose today (attachment: AuroraEdge_PROPOSED_AMENDMENT_v3.pdf):
1) Staged commit: 3-month onramp: 40% of target in months 1–2, 70% in month 3, full target month 4 onwards. We can map actual token/embedding units to the baseline in the amendment.
2) Temporary rate guard: a fixed per-token effective price for months 1–6 (6-month price hold) — rate increases after month 6 capped to a pre-agreed schedule tied to the final committed rate.
3) Onboarding credit: one-time $45,000 credit triggered when AuroraEdge completes the production traffic switch (operational milestone checklist in the attachment).
4) Renewal term: 12 months with a right to request a one-time mid-term true-up if usage exceeds 150% of committed cadence in any month.

Operational notes: we will need your projected month-by-month usage (a short forecast) to size the commit tiers and set the burst/overage paths. I've attached a template (AE_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4_2027.xlsx) — if you fill that we can finalize the numbers.

Ben and Laura are cc'd for commercial and finance alignment — Ben, can you confirm availability to lock these numbers if AuroraEdge confirms by next Friday?

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@auroraedge.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — looking for a safe ramp

Maya — quick commercial note from our side.

We can do the staged commit and 6-month price guard as described. A couple of considerations:
- The one-time onboarding credit is fine but we'd like to split it: $30k applied as an invoice credit at the start and the remaining $15k released after the production readiness milestone. That reduces billing churn on our invoicing side.
- For the true-up carve, instead of a hard 150% threshold causing renegotiation, can we adopt a tiered overage schedule: 0–125% of committed usage = normal overage rates; 125–175% = elevated overage; >175% triggers a mid-term commit review. That gives both sides predictable economics.
- We'll need a short SLA excerpt included in the amendment around latency percentiles for committed routes (so your SREs can route critical traffic).

If AuroraEdge is comfortable with the split credit and tiered overage, we can mark this commercial sketch as 'approved in principle' and drop the amendment into DocuSign for signature.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 11:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Samir Rao <samir@auroraedge.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@auroraedge.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — looking for a safe ramp

Thanks Stephanie / Ben — we reviewed the proposed amendment and the split-credit approach works for us. A few clarifying points before we sign:

1) On the staged commit, can the ramp be tied to our monthly submitted forecast (we'll send the completed AE_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4_2027.xlsx by EOD Friday)? We want the percentages to be semantically tied to forecasted baseline so we're not hit by an unexpectedly high starting month.

2) The 6-month price guard is acceptable. Please confirm the guard price will be the current effective per-token rate listed in the amendment PDF (line item 2.a).

3) Regarding the SLA excerpt — we'll accept Redwood's standard p95 latency target for the committed routes. Please attach the exact SLA language to the DocuSign envelope.

If you can confirm those three items and send the DocuSign link we will route for signature on our side.

Samir Rao
VP Engineering | AuroraEdge
samir@auroraedge.ai
